messages.subject: Zipf distribution
parts: I notice that there is no mention of the Zipf distribution in the Stan user's manual. Is it possible to approximate this distribution by any transformation of a differently distributed random variable?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Zipf distribution
parts:
It's easy to implement for a fixed power (see the chapter on
implementing custom probability functions), but we don't have
the Riemann zeta function implemented (yet), so it's not possible to do it
for varying parameters.

If you can deal with a continous approximation, there's the Pareto
distribution in Stan.

Boost provides Riemann zeta,

http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_55_0/libs/math/doc/html/math_toolkit/zetas/zeta.html

so we could add it directly with auto-diff. But auto-diffing these numerical
approximations to functions isn't ideal.

Plus, we really need log(zeta(s)) for Stan, and then we'd want a direct scheme
for evaluating both

log(zeta(s)

and

d/ds log(zeta(s)) = 1/zeta(s) d/ds zeta(s).

Sounds like a job for Michael :-)

- Bob
